overall: The AG found the Beverly Regional Airport Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by barring a no-trespass subject from its meetings from December 2018 through April 2019, and ordered future compliance; no further remedy since meetings moved to City Hall.

allegations.summary: A member of the public barred from airport property by a no-trespass notice alleged the commission denied him access to its public meetings after he requested to attend.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that from December 2018 through April 2019, the Commission denied the Complainant access to its meetings in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The complaint also challenged the airport's no-trespass notice itself and asked that it be vacated.
allegations.key_passage: Our jurisdiction is limited to enforcing the Open Meeting Law, so we do not review whether the Notice of No Trespass was properly issued in the first instance, nor are we empowered to vacate the Notice, as the Complainant requests.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law (940 CMR 29.02).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
